sl-interviews.caption: figures.sl-interviews.caption
sl-interviews.text: Interview synthesis: 14 product owners One interview per team, 45 minutes, same questions · main reason per owner 11 of 14 would involve UX earlier if they knew what they would get and when NO SLOT IN THE PLAN UX arrives as a favour at the end “Our quarter is planned before design hears about it.” P1 (Permits) “We’d book UX if there were a slot to book.” P2 (Payments) “Design comes after the sprint plan, every time.” P3 (Social services) “I never know when it’s too early to ask.” P4 (Permits) “There is no line for UX in our roadmap.” P5 (Payments) SCOPE FEAR early design might change the promise “Early design changes what we promised.” P6 (Payments) “A late ticket feels safer.” P7 (Social services) “Research might move our deadline.” P8 (Permits) NO NAME nobody knows who picks it up “Who is our designer, actually?” P9 (Social services) “Every ticket gets someone new.” P10 (Permits) “I don’t know whom to call.” P11 (Payments) WOULD NOT little to gain, or fewer meetings “Internal tool, a handful of users.” P12 (Internal tools) “Back-office screens; nobody complains.” P13 (Internal tools) “Honestly: fewer meetings, please.” P14 (Social services) would involve UX earlier would not P = product owner · cluster in brackets SEILSCHAFT · FICTIONAL EXAMPLE · FIG. 2

sl-steering-onepager.caption: figures.sl-steering-onepager.caption
sl-steering-onepager.text: Steering board · Digital Services Hochmatt Informatik · 2021 From a service desk to a UX practice A staged ask: grow only as far as the evidence carries us. THE PROBLEM, IN OUR OWN TICKETS 64% of requests arrive two weeks or less before release 420 h of rework after release in the last year 11 of 14 product teams have never met a designer THE STAGED ASK HIRE · THEN CHECK One intake for every request within six months. HIRE · THEN CHECK A named designer for the four teams with the most citizen traffic. REVIEW · MONTH 12 The board decides: grow the practice, or stop where it is. Head of Digital Services APPROVED SEILSCHAFT · FICTIONAL EXAMPLE · FIG. 1
